regime_context: TSX themes are broadly eligible (11/16) with Big Banks dominating on momentum rank but flagged as crowded; no single narrative. The absolute-trend gate historically cuts drawdowns here, while Technology/Gold/Silver/Uranium sit below it. Macro backdrop is noisy (AI/tech headlines dominate, unscheduled surprise share 0.59), adding event risk.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks lead on eligibility and momentum rank, and while rank is not a return forecast, the absolute-trend gate (the one validated risk-control edge in this market) keeps it in a stay-long zone. Crowding (z 1.76) is a size-down caution, not a fade signal. Durability is moderate (0.74, mixed Hurst), suggesting trend health is not yet deteriorating.
evidence: gate_helps=true (absolute-trend gate validated for drawdown control)
theses.dissent: Crowding and a high unscheduled-surprise macro backdrop raise the risk of a sharp sentiment reversal; cross-sectional momentum rank-IC is historically near zero, so trend persistence is not a reliable edge.

falsifier.text: Big Banks' durability_bar falls below 0.6 OR it loses eligibility (absolute trend breaks).

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology (XIT.TO) is ineligible under the absolute-trend gate, which is the single validated risk-control mechanism in this market. Historically, below-gate themes experienced higher volatility and deeper drawdowns. With high unscheduled surprise risk, avoiding ineligible themes is prudent.
evidence: gate_helps=true (trend gate validated for drawdown control)
theses.dissent: A macro catalyst (e.g., AI capex acceleration) could drive an explosive mean-reversion back above the trend, causing avoidance to miss a sharp rally.

falsifier.text: Technology becomes eligible (absolute trend flips above gate).

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
